dedupe_keys.name: us national infrastructure protection plan nipp 2013 partnering for critical infrastructure security and resilience

description: The National Infrastructure Protection Plan 2013, Partnering for Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience, sets out how government and the private sector work together to manage risks to US critical infrastructure and strengthen its security and resilience. It evolved from the original 2006 plan, revised in 2009, and meets the requirements of Presidential Policy Directive 21 (February 2013), with stakeholders from all 16 critical infrastructure sectors; its vision is of physical and cyber infrastructure that stays secure and resilient, with vulnerabilities reduced, consequences minimised and response and recovery hastened. CISA's page provides the plan and supplements on connecting to the national coordinating centres, executing a risk management approach, incorporating resilience into infrastructure projects (2013), and a threat information sharing framework (2016), plus FEMA Emergency Management Institute training courses, all free. Caveats: it is a framework document without data, and the 2024 NSM-22 memorandum calls for a biennial National Infrastructure Risk Management Plan to take its place. It supports scoping of sector interdependencies and risk management processes that simulation studies of critical infrastructure feed; a related record is the NSM-22 critical infrastructure memorandum.
